$schema_comment: Curated catalog of upstream MCP servers that pair well with memex. Each entry is a template that `memex upstream install <id>` can drop into ~/.memex/upstreams.json. Categories help users discover by need.

entries.name: filesystem
entries.description: Read/write files within an allowlist of directories. The single most-used MCP.

entries.name: git
entries.description: git operations on a local repo: status, diff, log, commit, branch.

entries.name: github
entries.summary: GitHub API: PRs, issues, commits, search, releases.
entries.long_description: The official GitHub MCP server. Lets your AI agent read and write to repositories you have access to: open issues, comment on PRs, search code across all your repos, fetch CI status, manage releases. Runs locally as an npx subprocess and authenticates with a Personal Access Token you control.
entries.memex_value: Behind the memex gateway, every github.* call your AI makes is captured as a tool_call episodic event. Over a week of usage that becomes a queryable history: which PRs the AI reviewed, which files it searched, which issues it touched. v0.7's consolidation pass promotes patterns into facts ("this user's PRs are 80% squash-merged", "engineering rejects PRs without tests"). Pair with `skill:github-pr-hygiene` so the AI runs basic checks before opening a PR.
setup_steps: Generate a Personal Access Token at https://github.com/settings/tokens
Grant scopes: `repo` (full control of private repos), `workflow` (read CI status), optionally `read:org`
Restart your AI client (Claude Code / Cursor / Windsurf) to pick up the new tools

usage_examples.what: Create an issue in a repo
usage_examples.example: create_issue(owner='quefly', repo='memex', title='HTTP upstream support', body='...')

usage_examples.what: Search code across all repos you have access to
Fetch a PR with reviews + status checks
Leave a PR review with line-level comments
List recent CI runs for a workflow

entries.name: github-remote
entries.summary: GitHub's official remote MCP server — no local subprocess.
entries.long_description: The hosted MCP endpoint operated by GitHub. Same tool surface as the local `github` server, but runs entirely on GitHub's infrastructure — no `npx`, no `node_modules/`, no local subprocess to supervise. Authenticates with a fine-grained PAT or OAuth token. Slightly higher latency per call but zero local footprint and no upgrade ceremony when the toolset evolves.
entries.memex_value: Same auto-capture as the local server — every call your AI makes flows through the memex gateway and lands as an episodic event. Use this variant when you want the smallest local footprint (cloud-laptop scenarios, ephemeral dev containers) or when the local npx-based server is failing to start. Pair with the same skills as `github`.
setup_steps: Generate a fine-grained Personal Access Token at https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens
Restrict scope to the specific repos your AI should touch — fine-grained is safer than classic PATs
Restart your AI client to pick up the new tools

usage_examples.what: Same shape as the local github server
Same shape; runs server-side on GitHub's infra

entries.name: gitlab
entries.description: GitLab API: MRs, issues, pipelines.

entries.name: fetch
entries.description: HTTP fetch with markdown extraction. Useful for reading docs, blog posts, API specs.

entries.name: puppeteer
entries.description: Browser automation via Puppeteer. Navigate, screenshot, click, evaluate.

entries.name: playwright
entries.description: Browser automation via Playwright. More robust than Puppeteer for cross-browser testing.

entries.name: sqlite
entries.description: Query a local SQLite database. Schema introspection + read/write.

entries.name: postgres
entries.description: Query a Postgres database (read-only by default). Schema introspection + select.

entries.name: slack
entries.description: Slack: send messages, list channels, read history.

entries.name: linear
entries.description: Linear issue tracker: create, update, search issues.

entries.name: notion
entries.description: Notion: read/write pages, search, databases.

entries.name: gdrive
entries.description: Google Drive: search files, read content, list folders.

entries.name: memory
entries.description: Reference: Anthropic's basic key-value memory. Useful contrast — memex is the structured-graph version.

entries.name: time
entries.description: Current time and timezone conversions. Cheap dependency.

entries.name: kubernetes
entries.description: kubectl-style operations against a configured kubeconfig context.

entries.name: aws
entries.description: AWS CLI wrapper. Read-only by default; write requires explicit allow.

entries.name: sentry
entries.description: Sentry: fetch issue details, stack traces. Useful for debugging from chat.

entries.name: gcp
entries.description: Google Cloud Platform: gcloud-equivalent CLI access via MCP. IAM, Cloud SQL, Cloud Run, BigQuery, GCS.
requires: gcloud auth configured OR service-account JSON via GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS

entries.name: cloudflare
entries.description: Cloudflare: Workers, KV, D1, R2, DNS, Zone configuration. Aligns with AuthFI URL topology.

entries.name: gmail
entries.description: Gmail: read/search/draft/send mail. Make 'what did I commit to via email last week' answerable.
requires: one-time OAuth via the server's auto-auth flow

entries.name: google-calendar
entries.description: Google Calendar: list/create/update events. Bridges chat decisions into your schedule.
requires: one-time OAuth via the server's auto-auth flow

entries.name: stripe
entries.description: Stripe: customers, subscriptions, invoices, payments. Read-only by default via Restricted Key.
requires: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY env var (use a Restricted Key, not a live secret)

entries.name: honeycomb
entries.description: Honeycomb: query traces and metrics. Connect production observability to chat.

entries.name: anthropic-console
entries.description: Anthropic Console: usage, billing, project state, organization settings. Track your own AI spend.
requires: ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_API_KEY env var (different from regular API key)

entries.name: filesystem-readonly
entries.description: Read-only filesystem within an allowlist. Lower-blast-radius alternative to `filesystem`.
